# Images that the release scan (publish.yml) and the nightly scan
# (nightly-image-scan.yml) scan and report, but that do NOT fail on a HIGH or
# CRITICAL finding.
#
# This file exists so that every exemption is visible in one place, and so that
# a pull request which adds one changes a file whose only subject is exemptions.
# A `blocking: false` buried in a matrix is easy to miss in review.
#
# An image belongs here only when BOTH of these hold:
#
#   1. No branch here can make the job green on its own — either because the
#      whole finding set is owned outside this repository, or because a part of
#      it is and that part alone still fails the threshold.
#   2. There is a recorded path that ends the exemption.
#
# Criterion 1 used to read "the finding set is owned outside this repository",
# full stop. It was widened, deliberately and visibly, for the former
# elitea-worker-python image (since deleted, together with its entry): most of
# its findings came from a Debian base with no fix published, while a smaller
# part was ours and fixable. Under the old wording that image had no honest
# home — it could not block (the base findings made every branch red) and it
# could not be exempt (the rest were ours). The wording now describes the mixed
# case, and an entry's retirement issue is what keeps it from being a hiding
# place: it names the fixable part, and the entry records exactly what is left
# and who owns it.
#
# Name both issues on the line above the entry: the findings, and the path that
# ends the entry. Delete the entry when that path completes.
#
# What an entry does NOT do:
#
#   - it does not change the HIGH,CRITICAL threshold;
#   - it does not suppress a CVE, and the full count is still printed;
#   - it does not relax the dormancy guards. A missing report, or a report
#     without the expected target type, still FAILS the job;
#   - it does not survive its cause. The job FAILS when an exempt image reports
#     zero findings, because the entry is then stale.
#
# publish.yml's `scan` matrix must set `blocking: false` for exactly these
# names. scripts/ci/image-matrix.sh (image-matrix.yml) fails when the two
# files disagree.
#
# Lines that start with # are comments. Blank lines are ignored.


# findings — #1330: the nightly scan of `latest` (4.58.0) on 2026-10-20
#   reported 147 HIGH or CRITICAL lines (1 CRITICAL, 146 HIGH), every one
#   "no fix yet" in Debian 13 (linux-libc-dev, python3.13, util-linux, curl,
#   ncurses, perl, systemd, acl, setuptools wheel). The image is
#   debian:trixie-slim plus build-essential, git, python3 and curl
#   (ADR-0034), the userland the agent's `run_command` needs to build a
#   user's project, so no branch here can clear it: criterion 1.
# retirement — the image stays a full Debian userland by design (decision 9:
#   the sandbox builds and tests the user's project). The entry ends when
#   Debian publishes fixes for the base findings, or when the workspace
#   sandbox moves to a minimal base with toolchains installed per project.
#   No retirement issue is filed yet; file it and name it here.
elitea-workspace-runner
